---
title: "Architecture: an interactive map of garry"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

garry is a lazy raster engine: verbs build an R-native compute graph,
a planner fuses it into schedulable stages, and executors run those
stages as XLA kernels (anvl traces each to a StableHLO program, pjrt
compiles it) over GDAL-read chunks (via gdalraster). This article maps
that structure interactively at two zoom levels. Both graphs are
generated by static analysis of the package sources
(`package-graph/build_graph.R` in the repository); nothing here is
hand-drawn. The pages embed a snapshot, so rerun the script below after
changing `R/`.

## The exported API surface

Every node below is an exported function, colour-coded by subsystem.
An edge `A -> B` means calling `A` reaches `B`, possibly through
internal code; edges to the gold triangle (anvl, the XLA compiler
frontend) and the green square (gdalraster, GDAL IO) show which verbs
ultimately touch which backend. Grey diamonds are other packages, among
them pjrt and stablehlo, the compile path for the kernels anvl traces.
Click a node to highlight its one-hop neighbourhood, use the dropdowns
to jump to a function or filter a subsystem, and scroll to zoom.

Two things are worth reading directly off this graph. First, the
lazy-verb layer (`lazy_map()`, `focal_map()`, `reduce_over()`, and
friends) reads no data and compiles nothing. While building, it reaches
anvl only to read a kernel's output dtype: an abstract trace when
`lazy_map()` or `scan_over()` has no `dtype`, or `reduce_over()` has a
custom reducer. Its pjrt edges come from fingerprinting arrays a kernel
body captures, which keys that dtype trace so a kernel repeated across
bands or slices traces once; nothing is compiled. Its other anvl edges,
such as `apply_mask()`'s, are the bodies of the kernels it builds,
which run at execution. Its one GDAL
edge is `shrink_footprint(boundary = "keep")`, which writes a
sourceless VRT marking the grid's interior. Second, pixels are read and
kernels run only by the execution verbs (`collect()`, `materialise()`,
`preview()`, `write_tif()`, `extract_points()`,
`lazy_value_and_grad()`, and the executors beneath them), which is the
lazy contract made visible; `plan_lazy()` reaches both backends to
prepare warped reads and kernels without running them. The other GDAL
edges read file headers and CRS definitions (`lazy_source()`,
`lazy_dataset()`, `grid_from_src()`, `grid_from_bbox()`), build tile
indexes and staged cubes, or set GDAL configuration. The other anvl
edges belong to the `g_*` vocabulary and the kernel bodies written in
it (`geomedian()`, `kalman_llt()`, `band_project()` and the like).

## The full internal call graph

The map below is the same analysis over every top-level definition in
the package: functions, S7 classes (boxes), generics (ellipses) and
methods (hexagons), with dashed edges for S7 dispatch. It exists for
contributors; users never need it, but it answers structural
questions quickly. Where does the anvl boundary sit? Every gold edge
originates in `ops.R` (the `g_*` vocabulary), as do the edges to pjrt
and stablehlo; a test enforces the rule for anvl and pjrt. Which
subsystems are large? Node size tracks line count, so
the scheduler and the GDAL adapter stand out immediately.

## Subsystems

The colour groups in both graphs correspond to the package's
subsystems:

- **IR & graph**: the node types, the `g_*` op vocabulary, the graph
  container, and the planner passes that fuse nodes into stages.
- **Grid & geometry**: `GridSpec`, chunk grids, and grid construction
  helpers. Every lazy object is pinned to a grid; planning is
  grid-identity-trivial by design.
- **Execution**: `collect()` down through the scheduler, daemon pool,
  the kernel programs sent to daemons, and the direct composite
  executors.
- **IO & GDAL**: the gdalraster adapter, dataset/STAC construction,
  HTTP authentication, and materialisation.
- **Models & kernels**: OmniCloudMask, the Kalman and Hampel
  smoothers, band projection, and dequantisers.
- **Viz & UX**: `plan_draw()`, `plan_view()`, `preview()`, and task
  reports.
- **Infra**: options and package start-up.

## Regenerating

Both graphs, plus a report of the exact anvl functions garry calls,
are rebuilt from source with:

```r
# from the package root
source("package-graph/build_graph.R")
```

The script parses `R/*.R` without evaluating it, so it runs on any
machine with `visNetwork`, `igraph` and `glue` installed.
